messages:
alice.s: FYI a customer in us-west reported streaming responses truncating mid-stream, then the client reconnects in ~20-40s. They see partial tokens and then a reconnect loop. request_id=rr-9b3c, session=kc-77
marcus.o: Any server logs or client logs we can grab? Error samples?
alice.s: Pasted the server-side proxy logs they sent — seems like write complaints then an abort:
```
[2026-03-15T18:02:11Z] proxy: sendmsg rr-9b3c -> client 10.2.3.45: EAGAIN
[2026-03-15T18:02:11Z] proxy: write_queue_size=8.2MiB > max_write_queue=8MiB
[2026-03-15T18:02:11Z] proxy: abort_stream rr-9b3c reason=slow_consumer
[2026-03-15T18:02:11Z] sse: stream_closed code=aborted
```
janelle.cs: Customer says their frontend does an incremental render and is intentionally reading very slowly (drops frames). They also saw billing jump for that session after retries.
priya.i: Kernel send buffer stats from that host? Could be socket sndbuf hitting limit + proxy buffering.
marcus.o: Do we have measurements of how long the client left the connection idle before reading more? Also what proxy is in front (envoy/nginx/sidecar)?
alice.s: They use CloudFront -> our edge -> envoy sidecar. Their frontend pauses reads for ~8-12s then drains a few hundred bytes. Pattern repeats.
marcus.o: That pattern is classic slow-consumer backpressure. Our proxy builds up queued chunks until we hit max_write_queue and abort to protect memory. Reconnects then cause partial output + duplicate billing if retries re-request tokens.
priya.i: Repro suggestion: run a local repro with a slow reader to confirm abort behavior. Example python consumer to intentionally read slowly:
```bash
# server: curl streaming endpoint
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream/rr-9b3c |
python3 slow_reader.py
```
# slow_reader.py
```python
import sys, time
for chunk in sys.stdin.buffer.raw.read().split(b\"\\n\\n\"):
    time.sleep(10)  # simulate paused render
    print(chunk.decode(errors='ignore'))
```
marcus.o: When you repro, look for EAGAIN / MSG_NOSIGNAL in proxy logs and the exact write_queue_size growth. We'll need that to tune defaults.
alice.s: I ran the repro on staging; got the same abort after ~8MB queued, envoy log: `connection: remote write buffer exceeded threshold, aborting`
priya.i: Short-term mitigations for customer: 1) advise client to keep socket reads/keepalive pulses (drain at least 1KB every 3s), 2) disable CloudFront response buffering (so bytes get through), 3) set a conservative reconnect/backoff to avoid duplicate requests.
janelle.cs: For billing concern — how are repeated partial streams billed? They were charged for the initial token generation before abort, and again on retry. Customer wants credits if we double-billed.
marcus.o: We bill on final accepted tokens currently. But retries that complete will be billed. For aborts that cut mid-response we sometimes still commit token usage. Escalate to billing to review rr-9b3c session trace.
support-bot: @billing-team please review session rr-9b3c for double billing with customer janelle.cs CC.
marcus.o: Long term fixes: - Make proxy drop oldest queued chunks instead of abort when queue near limit, and emit partial-close event so client can rehydrate without duplicate billing. - Add configurable per-customer max_queue_bytes and backpressure policy. - Add server-side early-heartbeat to nudge slow readers (0-length ping events).
priya.i: Also consider increasing default max_write_queue to 16MiB for dedicated customers with known slow-consumer workloads. But that increases memory usage.
alice.s: I've documented repro steps and attached staging traces in the ticket. I'll include recommended client changes and the CloudFront config steps.
janelle.cs: Sharing suggested copy for customer support message: "We're investigating a streaming abort due to slow client reads; short-term workaround: disable buffering at the edge and add small periodic reads / keepalives in your app. We're reviewing billing for the affected session."
marcus.o: Good. I'll open a follow-up engineering ticket for the proxy behavior changes and tag infra + runtime. Prioritize as P2.
alice.s: Thanks — will update customer when billing team responds. :thumbsup:
